page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre. Verse epigram in italic lines at top, then a rule, then a title block in larger roman and italic type, a heading "PROGNOSTICON.", then a verse poem in two-line stanzas with an initial "I", closing with "CL." at the lower right. No margin notes.

p.i: Fuderit (hæc siquidem pādere sacra nefas, Eccce manus medias inter (si credere fas est) Vera caro euadit qui modò panis erat. Non igitur te Pontificem nunc dixero, Verum Carnificem, & patrem dixero carnificum.

main_text.l: In nouam illam, & seculis omnibus supe- riribus inauditam stellam, cum illa carnificina Gallica nefandissima exor- tam, AVgusto mense, Anno Domini. 1572,
main_text.head: PROGNOSTICON.
main_text.p: Iste nouus nullo metuendus crine Cometes, Et radians puro cui nitet igne iubar: Ecquid portendat terris, Deus ille deorum Novit, & ostendent tempore fata suo. Quòd si humana aliquid possūt praescisceře mètes, Talia rimari nec mihi signa nefas, Fallor ego, aut ille est Ieffaam qualis in Orbem Duxit ab Eoo qui prius orbe Magos. Et qui nascenti praeluxit, nunciat idem Ecce reduxreducem rursus adesse Deum. Huic igitur felix, ô turba applaude piorum, Herodes, caueas tu tibi quisquis eris.

page.notes: Decorative rule and small ornaments throughout. Some words in the title block are set in mixed roman and italic type and are transcribed as best read. Passages "Ecquid", "Quòd", "mètes", "Ieffaam" and "reduxreducem" are doubtful and may contain printing errors. The running head and the poem line "Ecce reduxreducem" are reproduced as printed; the line "Fuderit" opens the epigram.
